subject: physics
question_text: Which is greater, limiting friction or kinetic friction? Give the reason.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The answer
lines: Limiting friction is greater than kinetic
So for the same pair of surfaces,
steps.why: This is why a heavy box is hard to start and then noticeably easier to keep sliding.
common_mistakes: Saying they are equal because both use the same normal force.

recall.must_convey: That limiting friction is greater than kinetic friction, so mu s is greater than mu k.
accept: mu s is greater than mu k

steps.memory_tip: Steel on steel gives about μ_s = 0.74 against μ_k = 0.57. Static is the larger number.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Commit to limiting friction in the first line, then write μ_s > μ_k.

steps.label: The reason
lines: While the body is at rest the two surfaces
settle into each other and the contact
points join. Once sliding starts there is
less time for those joins to form, so less

lines.text: Harder to start than to keep going

steps.why: Friction comes from contact at the microscopic high points, and those need time to form — which is the whole difference between the two coefficients.
common_mistakes: Explaining it by "the body has gained speed", which is not the reason.

recall.must_convey: That at rest the surfaces settle and the contact points join, and sliding gives them less time to form.

steps.memory_tip: Nothing about the body changes. What changes is how long the contacts had to form.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The reason is the contact points, not the speed the body has gained.

insider_note: Which is greater is one mark, the reason is the other. Answering μ_s > μ_k and stopping answers only half the question.
